name: Barak

sink.name: Bay of Bengal, via the Surma-Kushiyara-Meghna system

did_you_know: The Barak is Northeast India's second-largest river system after the Brahmaputra, and drains an entirely separate basin that never physically joins it.
At Haritikar in Assam's Karimganj district, the Barak splits into the Surma and Kushiyara before entering Bangladesh — it never reaches the sea as a single named channel.
Its Assam stretch is designated National Waterway 6, a key inland transport link for the landlocked Barak Valley.
